observation.visible_scene: A wide seascape at low sun (sunset/sunrise). The upper half is a pale pastel sky with thin, layered cirrus and a small dark cloud clump sitting on the horizon in front of the sun's warm glow; the lower half is the open ocean, with the sun's reflection forming a soft vertical bright band on the water. In the immediate foreground a line of breaking wave/white foam runs across the bottom of the frame. The horizon and cloud positions stay fixed throughout, indicating a static camera.
visible_changes: The initial broad band of white foreground foam (frame 1) gradually lowers toward the bottom edge and thins out over the first ~10 frames, leaving a smoother, more reflective water surface in the lower third.

From roughly frame 15 onward a new swell/crest rises in the lower foreground: a dark wave line with patchy white foam climbs from near the bottom edge toward the middle-lower frame and grows taller and more defined through frame 41.
The distant open-water surface shows only subtle, slow ripple/reflection changes; no large object moves across the horizon.
The sky, clouds, horizon line and the sun's reflection band remain essentially unchanged in position (camera is static; the moving bright band is a reflection of the low sun, not a separate object).
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the rising foreground swell eventually breaks or recedes after the last frame, and what wave cycle produced the foam seen at the very start.
Any motion or events outside this ~2.7 s window (the clip is a temporal crop with arbitrary endpoints).
uncertain_details: The exact phase relationship between the receding foam and the rising swell (whether they are the same wave cycle or two successive waves) is not fully resolvable from the sampled frames.
Minor handheld jitter of the camera cannot be entirely ruled out, but the background evidence (fixed horizon and clouds) supports a largely static viewpoint.
